passage:
Disha kept replaying a game level in her head during maths, and when the bell rang for games time she would rather have stayed at the tablet. Her mother, Jaya, noticed she got upset whenever she was told to stop. They agreed on a timer and outdoor play after dinner, and Disha found she could stop when it rang.

She and her friend Jagdish were racing for the top of the class leaderboard. When Jagdish moved ahead, Disha sulked and deleted his chat message. Then she thought: it is only a score. She took a break, walked round the building, and later typed, "Rematch tomorrow? Good game." Jagdish sent back a thumbs-up.

The game kept flashing offers: "Get the golden armour!" Disha wanted it to look cool. She asked Jaya first, who said not for now and explained that the game is made to tempt. Disha remembered that Jagdish never cared what she wore in the game.

After one bad loss, a stranger wrote, "You okay? Tough round." Disha felt warm at that. She wrote "thanks, I'm okay" and nothing about where she lived or her school, then told Jaya about it.

qa.q: What did Disha type to Jagdish after her break?
How did Jaya respond when Disha got upset about stopping, compared with when Disha wanted the golden armour?
qa.a: When Disha got upset at being told to stop, Jaya agreed on a timer and outdoor play after dinner; when Disha asked about the armour, Jaya said not for now and explained that the game is made to tempt.

qa.q: What was Disha feeling when Jagdish moved ahead on the leaderboard?
qa.a: She felt sulky and jealous, so she deleted his chat message before taking a break.

qa.q: Why was it wise for Disha to ask Jaya before buying the golden armour?
qa.a: The game is made to tempt, and Jaya could say no for now and explain why.

grounding: One child's time with an online game includes being unable to stop, a fierce rank race with a friend, purchase offers, and a stranger's kind message.
